messages.content:
The `CSVPrinter.printRecord` method takes an `Iterable` of values and prints each value by iterating over them. If any value in the record is `null`, it may be printed as "null" in the output.

Given this information, the issue may lie in the way the record values are passed to the `CSVFormat.format` method. When calling `CSVFormat.format("A", "B")`, if any of the supplied arguments are `null`, they will be printed as "null" in the output.

To fix this issue and prevent "null" from being appended to the output, the input values passed to `CSVFormat.format` should be validated to ensure that they are not `null` before formatting the CSV record.

The likely root cause of the bug is passing `null` values to the `CSVFormat.format` method. A validation check should be added to handle `null` values appropriately.

Now, I will provide the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.format(java.lang.Object...)
```
